reason: E1 shows that ~2 at% oxygen can strengthen some refractory HEAs with ductility, but the specific mechanism of ordered complexes and their effect on phase boundary stability, creep, and corrosion in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 are not directly supported by the cited evidence; E2 warns that oxygen can cause phase segregation and property degradation, which contradicts the claimed benefits.
premises: Oxygen additions of ~2 at% can substantially strengthen refractory HEAs while maintaining ductility
Ordered oxygen complexes form in the lattice and act as strong obstacles to dislocation motion
Oxygen complexes stabilize phase boundaries and reduce corrosion initiation sites
The AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA can be processed with controlled oxygen doping to form these complexes
Improved dislocation pinning and phase boundary stability will enhance high-temperature creep and corrosion resistance
